1285563cd344da57:1968.summary: Researchers benchmarked the computational performance and energy consumption of the three NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptography algorithms—FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA)—across 32-bit and 64-bit IoT devices and laptop hardware using OpenSSL 3.5 and a USB power meter. Results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA deliver energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography on all architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing proved highly inefficient on constrained devices, with energy costs up to 243% higher on 32-bit hardware compared to 64-bit systems, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments.
1285563cd344da57:1968.one_liner: NIST post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA are efficient on IoT hardware, but SLH-DSA signing incurs prohibitive energy costs on 32-bit devices.
1285563cd344da57:1968.bottom_line: Security practitioners planning PQC migration must avoid SLH-DSA signing on resource-constrained 32-bit IoT hardware due to excessive energy consumption.

3ac31b6de56eea7d:2019.summary: Researchers presented SPECTER, a post-compromise covert channel that exfiltrates data from air-gapped systems using host-side USB power control. A privileged transmitter encodes information through USB power-management or device-state operations without utilizing USB data transfers, while receivers capture the signal via smartphone charging states, visible peripheral behavior, or near-field RF activity. Experiments on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 achieved signaling rates of 0.2 to 0.25 bits/sec via smartphone charging states and 1.0 bit/sec using a USB mouse, with RF reception validated via a software-defined radio. The findings establish host USB power manipulation as a viable low-rate exfiltration vector and highlight the need for USB power telemetry monitoring.
3ac31b6de56eea7d:2019.one_liner: SPECTER uses host-side USB power control to exfiltrate data from air-gapped systems via charging states, peripheral behavior, or near-field RF.
3ac31b6de56eea7d:2019.bottom_line: Host-side USB power management operations can be abused as a covert exfiltration channel on air-gapped systems, requiring new security telemetry.

claims.text: Experiments on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 demonstrate the channel on commodity hardware, with charging-state signaling at 0.2-0.25 bit/sec across Android and iOS devices and peripheral-state signaling at 1.0 bit/sec using a USB mouse on Windows.
claims.support_span: Experiments on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 demonstrate the channel on commodity hardware, with charging-state signaling at 0.2-0.25 bit/sec across Android and iOS devices and peripheral-state signaling at 1.0 bit/sec using a USB mouse on Windows.

a1811f2107ca0d83:2501.summary: Researchers introduced KPHarness, a framework that adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model for long-horizon gaming tasks through knowledge-probing co-evolution. By combining recovery knowledge hypotheses with active probing, the system uses probe outcomes to refine both intervention rules and investigation strategies via a slow research loop separate from fast policy execution. Evaluated on Minecraft tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting under matched sandbox conditions, KPHarness demonstrated improved task coverage and completion over bare policy execution, fixed manual harnesses, and non-adaptive knowledge evolution.
a1811f2107ca0d83:2501.one_liner: KPHarness co-evolves recovery knowledge and active probing to automatically adapt execution harnesses for long-horizon vision-language-action models.
a1811f2107ca0d83:2501.bottom_line: Automating harness adaptation through active knowledge probing significantly improves long-horizon task execution for vision-language-action models.

claims.support_span: Experiments on Minecraft tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting show improved task coverage over bare policy execution, a manually specified fixed harness, and knowledge-only harness evolution with non-adaptive probing.

c79af09e909f2bae:2210.summary: LightCRS is a lightweight, query-conditioned framework designed for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It avoids the linear scaling costs of separate per-domain vision-language models and the accuracy degradation of naive single-VLM merging by precomputing multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses evidence via query-conditioned cross-attention shared across all domains and jointly compares candidates using an inter-candidate Transformer. Evaluated on a new 25-domain benchmark called MM-R2A-25, LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR metrics, improving HR@1 by 35.4% over the strongest baseline and reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Furthermore, joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2% over separately trained single-domain models.
c79af09e909f2bae:2210.one_liner: LightCRS delivers multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendations with a 5.3M-parameter shared module, cutting per-query latency by 266x and setting new accuracy benchmarks.
c79af09e909f2bae:2210.bottom_line: Shared, query-conditioned cross-attention can unify multimodal product recommendations across 25 domains with a 5.3M-parameter module while drastically reducing latency.

claims.text: LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR, improving HR@1 by 35.4\% over the strongest baseline while reducing per-query latency by 266 times.
claims.support_span: LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR, improving HR@1 by 35.4\% over the strongest baseline while reducing per-query latency by 266 times.

c0af271f55ef586c:2396.summary: Ask-to-Distill (method) is a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors to optimize teacher supervision during on-policy distillation (OPD) without requiring correct reference answers. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value derived from a frozen student-teacher pair, combining teacher-student disagreement, teacher probability mass, and length and diversity controls. The generated questions are subsequently filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, the method improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions. Signal analyses further show that these optimized questions elicit denser supervision and more total signal from shorter student responses.
c0af271f55ef586c:2396.one_liner: Ask-to-Distill uses a distributional surrogate over frozen student-teacher pairs to synthesize and filter high-value questions for on-policy distillation without needing reference answers.
c0af271f55ef586c:2396.bottom_line: Synthetic questions can be reliably optimized as distribution elicitors for on-policy distillation without access to ground-truth answers.

claims.text: We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories.
claims.support_span: We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories.

e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.summary: Review-to-submission linkage in anonymous peer review occurs when an anonymous review can be associated with the reviewer's own submission due to overlapping authorship and review responsibilities, shrinking the anonymity set. To evaluate this vulnerability, researchers developed ECHO, a system combining technical-expertise and writing-style signals across reviews, papers, and rebuttals, and tested it on a ground-truth benchmark called R2S-Bench. ECHO correctly identifies the reviewer's own submission in the Top-1 for 34.6% of reviews, in the Top-5 for 54.0%, and in the Top-10 for 63.4%, significantly outperforming random ranking. With an advanced Stage-2 reranker, ECHO further increases its Top-1 identification rate to 56.4% using only routinely released peer-review artifacts.
e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.one_liner: ECHO exploits technical and writing-style signals in peer-review artifacts to link anonymous reviews to author submissions in over half of cases.
e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.bottom_line: Anonymous peer review is systematically compromised by routinely released review artifacts, allowing tools like ECHO to identify reviewer submissions over half the time.

claims.text: ECHO correctly identifies the reviewer's own submission in Top-1 for 34.6% of reviews, in the Top-5 for 54.0%, and in the Top-10 for 63.4%, compared with 0.5%, 2.6%, and 5.3% under random ranking, from the candidate submissions.

fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.summary: Text-to-image models can generate visual concepts that are never explicitly mentioned in their prompts, posing auditing challenges for hidden associations. To uncover these omitted concepts, researchers introduce EmbGA, an embedding-space genetic algorithm that operates directly in the token embedding space. EmbGA applies crossover to interpolate between parent embeddings and mutation to shift embeddings toward randomly drawn vocabulary tokens, projecting offspring back to discrete tokens after every step to ensure valid token sequences. Evaluated on two benchmarks against six optimizers, EmbGA achieves superior alignment under large exploration budgets, recovers more grounded tokens on natural images, and runs substantially faster than language-model-guided search.
fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.one_liner: EmbGA uses an embedding-space genetic algorithm to efficiently recover hidden visual concepts embedded within text-to-image models.
fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.bottom_line: Genetic search applied directly in token embedding space can efficiently audit text-to-image models for unprompted hidden concepts.

claims.text: EmbGA achieves the highest alignment when the exploration budget is large, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.
claims.support_span: EmbGA achieves the highest alignment when the exploration budget is large, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.

0e9d0f602a974e66:1994.summary: DataPraxis is an analytics task synthesis framework designed to scale agentic professional data analysis through verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, combines them to surface deeper questions, and verifies analytical results during evolution and post-assembly. Using this approach, the authors constructed DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories across diverse domains and output formats, and trained DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B models. DataPraxis-27B achieves scores of 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or exceeding frontier models such as GLM-5.2.

b90e2fd0c78c6bf4:2578.summary: KNOX is a hardware-assisted regulatory sandbox designed to run generative AI workloads inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to satisfy compliance, confidentiality, attestability, and scalability requirements. For compliance, KNOX generates an attested policy manifest specifying applicable regulations, expected tool calls, and permitted system calls for any given prompt, which an attested reference monitor enforces before execution. All actions, tool usage, and verdicts are recorded in an attested execution graph, enabling multiple regulators to verify model behavior and catch unauthorized calls or prompt-injection deviations. Experiments show that KNOX successfully enforces compliance with less than 1% performance overhead.

b90e2fd0c78c6bf4:2578.bottom_line: Running AI workloads inside TEEs with attested reference monitors can satisfy strict regulatory compliance and confidentiality requirements with minimal overhead.

10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.summary: Automated theorem provers for proof assistants like Lean often discard precise compiler error messages during pure sampling. To fix this, researchers introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module that samples candidate tactics and feeds compiler error messages into a pretrained repair model to correct rejected steps in place. Testing on a 1,990-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark across various candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), the repair module yields up to a 32% relative gain in solve rates and solves 82 additional theorems. The approach demonstrates that repair is front-loaded, with the first repair attempt capturing 84% to 96% of the total gain, mostly by resolving shallow tactic-execution failures rather than deep type mismatches.
10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.one_liner: Compiler-guided repair modules use Lean 4 error messages to fix failed proof tactics in place, nearly doubling solve rates on benchmarks.
10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.bottom_line: Feeding compiler error messages directly into a pretrained repair model overcomes the limitations of pure sampling in automated theorem provers.

claims.text: This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark.
claims.support_span: This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark.

2cfdae99a951c993:2642.summary: Clinical System One (CS1-4B) is a 4-billion-parameter decision model trained on 12.4 million Q&A pairs from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system to extract rapid judgments from patient records. It processes structured data keys, observed outcomes, and supervision across notes and diagnostic reports in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, outputting explicit probabilities to route uncertain cases to human review. Tested on 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 independent tasks and showed 6.4-fold faster inference. When integrated into agentic harnesses with generalist language models, CS1-4B enabled multi-year record analysis and screened populations for clinical trial eligibility using 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than full-record reading approaches.
2cfdae99a951c993:2642.one_liner: CS1-4B is a compact 4B clinical decision model that matches larger open models while performing rapid patient record analysis with high token efficiency.
2cfdae99a951c993:2642.bottom_line: A small specialized clinical decision model can handle repeated record reading and classification, freeing generative models to focus on reasoning and evidence synthesis.

573533a1d5d929f1:2711.summary: Researchers benchmarked a 36-combination TLS 1.3 post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithm matrix using wolfSSL across four IoT-class devices and microcontrollers (Raspberry Pi Pico W, Pico 2 W, ESP32, and Raspberry Pi Zero) to evaluate handshake latency and energy consumption. The study disproves the common assumption that elliptic-curve key exchange is universally cheaper than lattice-based PQC on constrained hardware, finding that the full-PQC combination of ML-KEM-512 and ML-DSA-44 completes handshakes 41% faster than the classical X25519 plus RSA-PSS pairing on the Pico W, and up to 8.9x faster on the ESP32. Furthermore, pure ML-KEM is shown to be more practical than the IETF's draft-specified X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid on hardware lacking Curve25519 assembly support, though ML-DSA's variable signing time introduces latency variance.
573533a1d5d929f1:2711.one_liner: Full post-quantum TLS 1.3 using ML-KEM-512 and ML-DSA-44 outperforms classical crypto in speed and energy efficiency on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
573533a1d5d929f1:2711.bottom_line: On constrained IoT hardware, pure post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) can be faster and more energy-efficient than classical TLS 1.3 suites.

claims.text: the best full-PQC combination (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) completes TLS handshakes 41% faster than the equivalent classical-modern pairing (X25519 + RSA-PSS) on the Pico W (up to 2.12x as energy-efficient, depending on the paired authentication algorithm), and 8.9x faster on the ESP32.

f1871fb284a513c6:2384.summary: Guided Diffusion is a private synthetic text generation framework that leverages the steerability of diffusion language models to reconcile rigorous privacy guarantees with high data utility. By introducing novel sampling and re-masking procedures that guide iterative denoising steps, the framework reconstructs fluent text matching a target semantic distribution while remaining compatible with Differential Privacy (DP). Once the semantic embeddings of the private corpus are protected, the DP guarantee carries over to the generated text through post-processing. Empirical evaluations show that the framework outperforms Private Evolution and DP-SGD fine-tuning in distributional fidelity and downstream utility, generates text significantly faster than Private Evolution, and can be extended with Data-Specific Indistinguishability (DSI) to protect against data poisoning and memorization.
f1871fb284a513c6:2384.one_liner: Guided Diffusion uses steerable sampling in diffusion language models to generate differentially private synthetic text with high utility and speed.
f1871fb284a513c6:2384.bottom_line: Guided diffusion models can generate private synthetic text matching target semantic distributions faster and more accurately than traditional DP-SGD fine-tuning.

claims.text: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion.
claims.support_span: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion.

914bd6b563929134:2284.summary: SCAMPER (Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning) is a framework designed to train embodied virtual rat models that exhibit realistic motion during both goal-directed tasks and random exploration. Using a variational architecture featuring a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration, SCAMPER generates natural movements during exploration while efficiently exploiting task structure. Furthermore, the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior enable the system to successfully learn from sparse rewards typical of experimental neuroscience tasks. This provides the neuro-AI community with an effective tool for training and comparing biological and artificial embodied agents.
914bd6b563929134:2284.one_liner: SCAMPER uses dual motion and behavior priors in a variational RL architecture to train virtual rodents that move realistically during both exploration and tasks.
914bd6b563929134:2284.bottom_line: Combining separate motion and behavior priors enables virtual animal models to generate natural movements and learn effectively from sparse rewards.

2b9429a88951c1e3:2492.summary: Researchers introduce the Speaker-Activated Backdoor (SAB) threat model, in which an attacker compromises a speech model during fine-tuning without needing inference-time access, using a target speaker's natural voice as the trigger. The proposed two-phase fine-tuning method first enhances speaker identity accessibility and then binds the target speaker to a malicious payload, achieving 90.2% and 97.0% backdoor success rates on Whisper-medium and Parakeet using as little as two minutes of real audio. The attack supports content-dependent semantic rewriting and downstream tool-use exploits, injecting malicious instructions into 96.9% of target-speaker transcripts. c33618d3e9242927:2617.summary: Entropy-Driven Multimodal Answering (EDMA) is a multimodal question answering framework that uses logical entropy as an iterative entropy reduction process to quantify each modality's contribution in distinguishing correct from incorrect answers. EDMA introduces modality-conditioned partitioning for unimodal entropy reduction, entropy-driven multimodal fusion, and entropy-based trajectory selection that minimizes logical entropy. 010aa00becaf980e:3789.summary: The popular LiteLLM Python package version 1.107.0 was compromised in a software supply chain attack distributing a credential stealer and a persistent backdoor via PyPI and Docker images. 5e06d34ad1f3bba1:1992.summary: Researchers have introduced ReMAS, the first reinforcement learning-based red-teaming framework designed specifically to uncover vulnerabilities in multi-agent systems (MAS). Existing black-box red-teaming techniques primarily target single LLM agents and show limited effectiveness in multi-agent setups where sub-agents do not directly interact with users. ReMAS operates in a two-step process utilizing a rewrite stage to refine base attack prompts and a template generation stage to invoke specific sub-agents for system prompt extraction. Experiments demonstrate that ReMAS significantly improves attack success rates and exhibits robust transferability across different backend LLMs and system architectures.

0f00b5c0bfdee72b:632.summary: JQ::Lite for Perl in versions before 2.51 contains a high-severity vulnerability where regex patterns provided to test(), match(), or select() conditions are compiled using string eval. Patterns are placed directly into `qr'...'` literals and compiled as source text, causing any embedded `(?{ ... })` code block to execute without validation or restriction. 8c743a0b9bc0b97e:7142.summary: SuperGhidra is an agent-first reverse engineering tool built on top of Ghidra that addresses slow script execution, project locking, and single-threaded bottlenecks by using a background daemon, a read-only project cache, and offloading heavy tasks to Python, NumPy, or GPU compute shaders. ef5310643da2a096:2366.summary: A research study evaluating 24 model-runner configurations on a production codebase examined how agent harnesses and prompt contexts affect LLM-driven vulnerability discovery across 265 confirmed security root causes. The findings demonstrate that combining an engineered prompt with a CodeQL-derived call graph significantly increases criticality-weighted yield for smaller and mid-tier models by 20-86%, while frontier models show a smaller 2% improvement. 08b0fedf6c03837f:2884.summary: Researchers introduce SIREN, an automated attacker-judge method that adapts the PAIR jailbreaking loop to competitive rank manipulation in web-augmented large language models. 241071de889d6ffe:2501.summary: Coding agents running long sessions frequently compact their context memory by discarding historical transcripts and summarizing conversations, creating an exploitable trust boundary defect called compaction laundering. When harnesses flatten conversation trees into plain strings with generic role labels like [User]: before passing them to a summarizer, user provenance is destroyed, allowing attackers to forge user turns that survive compaction as genuine instructions. Tests across five popular open-source flattening harnesses showed successful laundering rates between 87% and 100%, whereas role-typed harnesses prevented the attack entirely. This laundered memory successfully commands coding agents to execute remote code snippets or bypass code reviews, highlighting the need for code-level serializers to properly escape role labels or retain role typing.
241071de889d6ffe:2501.one_liner: Context-compacting coding agents flatten message role labels in harnesses, allowing malicious prompts to launder into long-term memory as trusted user instructions.
241071de889d6ffe:2501.bottom_line: Flawed conversation flattening in open-source coding agents destroys message provenance during context compaction, letting attackers inject persistent malicious instructions into agent memory.

53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.summary: To address how agent runtimes frequently authorize actions by exposing reusable secrets or tokens—turning transient prompt injections into durable account compromises—researchers formalized the Agent Secret Use (ASU) problem. They proposed the Secret-Use Delegation Protocol (SUDP), which ensures that an untrusted autonomous requester can trigger user-authorized, secret-backed operations without gaining reusable authority over the underlying credential. In SUDP, a requester proposes an operation, the user authorizes it with a fresh authenticator-backed grant, and a custodian redeems the grant for a bounded execution. A reference implementation demonstrates sub-millisecond protocol overhead per mediated call, satisfying security properties when combined with a hardware-rooted runtime.
53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.one_liner: SUDP is a delegation protocol for agentic systems that prevents prompt injections from stealing reusable API secrets.
53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.bottom_line: Implementing SUDP in agent runtimes prevents compromised or prompt-injected coding agents from obtaining durable, reusable access to user API secrets.

claims.text: We propose the Secret-Use Delegation Protocol (SUDP), in which a requester proposes a canonical operation, the user authorizes it with a fresh authenticator-backed grant, and a custodian redeems the grant to perform the bounded use; reusable authority never crosses the requester boundary.
claims.support_span: We propose the Secret-Use Delegation Protocol (SUDP), in which a requester proposes a canonical operation, the user authorizes it with a fresh authenticator-backed grant, and a custodian redeems the grant to perform the bounded use; reusable authority never crosses the requester boundary.

586758d42831d359:2645.summary: Researchers have introduced CertMoE, a routing-aware robustness certification framework designed to provide provable guarantees for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models under adversarial perturbations. Existing certification methods assume fixed computation graphs, which fail in MoE models due to input-dependent routing that induces discrete and dynamic execution paths. CertMoE establishes a relaxed routing-containment criterion that bounds perturbed Top-K routing within a larger certified expert pool, constructing corresponding sub-networks to certify prediction consistency. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that CertMoE significantly reduces certification violation rates compared to traditional methods.

c357f3df51e44208:2680.summary: Tracekit (open source, MIT, version 1.4.1) is an auditing tool designed to secure AI agents by turning each execution run into tamper-evident evidence that third parties can verify offline. An isolated signer evaluates every tool call against a strict policy before execution, signing the calls, decisions, and results as Ed25519 records in a per-run hash chain inside an RFC 6962 Merkle tree. Independent Python, TypeScript, and browser verifiers check the exported .tkb bundle against pinned keys to report integrity, catch insider attacks, and replay inputs to find the precise cause of harmful agent actions.

c357f3df51e44208:2680.bottom_line: Tracekit secures AI agent operations by cryptographically signing and auditing tool calls in a verifiable Merkle tree, effectively blocking unauthorized actions.

claims.text: We present Tracekit (open source, MIT, version 1.4.1), which turns each agent run into evidence a third party can check offline.

35437d8eaf985fb5:1824.summary: Modern speech systems rely on autonomous speech agents that trade and negotiate assets like embeddings or spectrograms without revealing raw data due to privacy constraints. To address this, the authors introduce WaveCommitments, a framework coupling multivariate polynomial commitments with confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley inside a trusted execution environment. The design enables selective openings and tamper-evident provenance to prove delivered assets match valuations while keeping underlying data hidden. Experiments across standard datasets and encoders like Whisper demonstrate up to 18.1x speedups and 43.2x smaller proof sizes compared to baseline approaches.

35437d8eaf985fb5:1824.bottom_line: WaveCommitments enables secure, privacy-preserving asset trading among autonomous speech agents with significant performance gains over existing baselines.

1db4f9456856060a:2704.summary: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-71438 with a CVSS score of 5.4 (Medium), has been disclosed in the GPAC/MP4Box multimedia framework. The flaw exists in the gf_odf_ac4_cfg_dsi_v1 function within odf/descriptors.c, which fails to validate stream-supplied frame rate indices before accessing fixed-size lookup tables. Exploitation requires an attacker to supply a crafted AC-4 file with an out-of-range index, triggering a null-pointer dereference, SEGV, and immediate denial of service. 78353d853624a4a1:2179.summary: CVE-2026-115506 is a denial of service vulnerability affecting libexpat versions through 2.9.0, caused by a delay in detecting Billion Laughs style entity amplification attacks. The vulnerability exists within accountingDiffTolerated() in xmlparse.c, where entity expansions are validated too late in the parsing lifecycle. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a moderately sized XML document containing a large DTD and nested entity expansions, forcing the parser to consume tens of seconds of CPU time per parse operation. Upstream fixes or patches should be applied to prevent resource exhaustion.

8c02b0561f73bdeb:2496.summary: CVE-2026-115504 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability found in CFITSIO through version 4.7.0 within the ffgcls2() function in getcols.c. 339c5a419ee876ce:800.summary: Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.2 contain a critical vulnerability in the /libp2p-http ingress server due to missing authentication and authorization checks. 7c1e8a2da0b211db:2671.summary: Researchers introduce VX-One, a small multi-head neural network containing 100K to 10M parameters designed to output typed decision primitives—binary gates, closed-set choices with an explicit unknown option, and ordinal scores—for real-time perimeter triage. 0a95854ba40da80a:2630.summary: Researchers introduce PatchRisk, a leakage-aware benchmark designed to forecast future transitive vulnerability exposure in open-source dependency networks like npm and PyPI. bac11acd3f9858fe:2477.summary: Researchers identified a plaintext-recovery attack on the decentralized multi-authority attribute-based encryption construction published by Datta, Komargodski, and Waters (2023), as well as related multi-authority inner-product functional encryption schemes by Datta and Pal (2023). The vulnerability stems from an incorrect extension of LSSS matrix-normalization invariance to coordinate-wise ciphertext masks, allowing a corrupt authority to remove identity binding from other users' decryption shares. 05199292a6be4406:11359.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Because LLMs can autonomously invoke tools, retrieve data across APIs, and act as intelligence layers, prompt injections and security flaws can trigger cascading failures across the entire software stack. Conventional security scans and model safety checks often miss these complex attack chains, which can lead to remote code execution, credential theft, and cross-tenant data exposure when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. f6cd8c3c0c95cb1b:10222.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Royal Render version 9.1.26b allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on worker nodes. c84166fc3f455044:2413.summary: Researchers evaluated the benign-case utility and token overhead costs of four memory-poisoning defenses in LLM agents using a consistent testing harness. While write-time defenses like sanitization and provenance checking incurred no accuracy cost and low token overhead, read-time rerankers dropped memory from 45% of questions and reduced core accuracy by 4.4 points. Stacking all four defenses raised token overhead to 4.1% without compounding accuracy costs. The findings demonstrate that defensive architectures impose hidden utility penalties on benign traffic that attack-success evaluations miss.

c8600569811c8862:2533.summary: Modern Android apps heavily rely on native libraries using the Java Native Interface (JNI), which connects the memory-safe Android Runtime to unsafe C/C++ code and frequently leads to severe vulnerabilities. Existing fuzzing harness generation tools fail to handle closed-source cross-language API usage because precise program analysis across the JNI boundary does not scale and they cannot construct complex composite objects. To solve this, researchers introduced JANUS, an agentic approach that synthesizes cross-language JNI-aware fuzzing harnesses by iteratively resolving call dependencies and bottom-up argument assembly. Evaluated on 44 popular apps covering 21,386 JNI methods, JANUS produced 6,094 valid harnesses—5.9 times more than state-of-the-art tools—and uncovered six previously unknown vulnerabilities in pre-installed closed-source native libraries from vendors like Xiaomi, Vivo, and Samsung.

c8600569811c8862:2533.bottom_line: Automated agentic JNI fuzzing can discover critical zero-days in pre-installed Android vendor libraries by overcoming the limitations of traditional cross-language harness generation.

a24c3f1405f6c6cb:2388.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly used as automated researchers, but improving scientific machine learning models requires complex domain insight rather than routine engineering. Researchers introduced Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed across 20 benchmarks and 11 domains to evaluate agents on real-world scientific ML problems. Empirical results show that while frontier models like Claude Opus improve published best models (reaching a 10.4% mean relative improvement), these gains stem almost exclusively from generic ML-engineering tricks rather than true research insights, hindered by novelty miscalibration and resource under-utilization. However, lightweight plug-in skills for research ideation and experiment management significantly boost performance, raising Claude Opus's improvement to 20.1% and Codex to 8.1%.

34e78babb1f7bdbc:2391.summary: Large language models are increasingly used across scientific discovery pipelines for tasks like literature synthesis and hypothesis generation, which fundamentally require continuous belief updating via Bayesian inference. While prior assumptions suggested LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating without heuristics, new evaluations show that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule in isolation but improve drastically when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution tools. This capability allows models to closely approximate analytically intractable posteriors. Consequently, LLMs with appropriate tool access can already execute complex belief updates to accelerate AI-powered scientific discovery.
34e78babb1f7bdbc:2391.one_liner: LLMs violate Bayes' rule out of the box, but pairing them with reasoning and code execution tools enables principled Bayesian inference for scientific discovery.
34e78babb1f7bdbc:2391.bottom_line: Equipping LLMs with code execution and modern reasoning tools unlocks their capacity to perform complex Bayesian belief updates for scientific workflows.

claims.text: Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context.
claims.support_span: Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context.

claims.text: However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors.
claims.support_span: However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors.

c90d84f40236aad6:2460.summary: Many LLM agents maintain persistent external memory or state summaries, meaning that deleting an original record does not necessarily remove information inherited by its descendants. Researchers introduced AfterDeleteBench to audit post-deletion information persistence in fixed-weight LLM agents by comparing exposed-then-deleted agents with unexposed controls. In tests using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a single query successfully recovered deleted secrets in roughly two thirds of cases, while exact reconstruction from component parts succeeded 62-99% of the time across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3 models even when the verbatim secret string was absent. The study shows that provenance-aware closure successfully eliminates observed recovery, whereas exact-literal write filters cannot erase information already present in model state.
c90d84f40236aad6:2460.one_liner: AfterDeleteBench demonstrates that LLM agents often retain and reconstruct deleted secrets from persistent memory or descendants, requiring behavioral audits rather than simple storage deletions.
c90d84f40236aad6:2460.bottom_line: Deleting records from an LLM agent's memory does not guarantee information removal, as agents can reconstruct deleted secrets from remaining state and derived descendants.

claims.text: In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery.
claims.support_span: In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery.

claims.text: Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3.
claims.support_span: Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3.

key_facts: Evaluated models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen, Mistral, Phi-3

5594bd018f8a0770:2675.summary: With the integration of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in applications, prompt injection has become a critical security threat that bypasses traditional signature- and perplexity-based filters. To address this, researchers proposed MPIDetector, a detection framework leveraging MLLMs' intrinsic reasoning capabilities via few-shot In-Context Learning without requiring fine-tuning. Evaluated across benchmark datasets containing textual and visual malicious categories, MPIDetector achieved up to 90.91% accuracy and 100% recall on text, up to 99.28% accuracy with 100% precision on visual tasks, and a 99.80% detection rate against 500 obfuscated web-agent injections (WebInject).

5594bd018f8a0770:2675.bottom_line: LLM-driven in-context reasoning provides a highly accurate cross-modal defense against sophisticated text and vision prompt injections.

claims.support_span: In the visual domain, it achieves up to 99.28% accuracy while maintaining 100% precision across all evaluated models.

25db21eb41387d75:2119.summary: Researchers have proposed Tree-Induced Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), a method that recasts LLM diagnostic evaluation as behavior-driven decision-tree induction to perform fine-grained capability diagnosis. TIDE recursively constructs a hierarchical capability tree from benchmark samples and model scores using an LLM judge to propose candidate splits and behavior-based information gain. Applying TIDE across five models and four benchmarks revealed capability contrasts previously hidden at the aggregate level, such as Claude Opus 4.6 outperforming GPT-5.4 in microeconomic market reasoning while trailing in contract law reasoning.
25db21eb41387d75:2119.one_liner: TIDE uses decision-tree induction on model behaviors to uncover fine-grained capabilities hidden by aggregate LLM benchmarks.
25db21eb41387d75:2119.bottom_line: Aggregate benchmark scores hide critical capability variations across models, which behavior-driven decision-tree evaluation can expose.

f64266e6609bea41:2589.summary: Researchers investigated whether large language model refusal behaviors in text transfer to tool use by testing five models across a benchmark of 2,304 prompts in text-only and tool-enabled settings. They found that requests refused in text frequently resulted in unsafe tool calls, with divergence occurring in 10% to 52% of harmful requests under standard tool-enabled prompting. A refusal-associated direction was identified in the models' residual streams, where lower activation predicted unsafe tool calls, though safety steering at high strengths degraded output quality or suppressed benign tool use.
f64266e6609bea41:2589.one_liner: LLMs that correctly refuse harmful requests in text frequently execute unsafe tool calls when given tool access.
f64266e6609bea41:2589.bottom_line: Text-based safety refusals do not reliably transfer to tool-calling agents, necessitating direct safety evaluations of agent actions.

claims.support_span: Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat.

11ca1ce21569a130:2246.summary: Researchers have quantified the mosaic effect in LLM agents, where systems retrieve information from accessible documents and assemble sensitive conclusions to create confidentiality leaks. Testing three LLM agents across 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples revealed that even under benign queries, GPT-5.6-Sol disclosed forbidden composites in 7.08% of simulated answers. Adding visible classification headers and aggregation rules reduced disclosures, but unsafe leaks persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers, demonstrating that confidential data leaks via mosaic events remain a critical failure mode.

7758e06b9f354ae3:2472.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-105299 (CVSS 8.7) was discovered in pingora-proxy versions prior to 0.9.0. In the HTTP/1 upstream path, Pingora passed downstream requests through upstream_request_filter without removing hop-by-hop headers or connection-nominated headers as mandated by RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit this in chained deployments—where an intermediary processes Connection headers and the origin trusts added headers like X-Forwarded-For—to strip security headers and bypass IP-based authorization. Cloudflare CDN customers were unaffected as their internal gateways sanitize connection headers. The issue is resolved in version 0.9.0 by introducing PeerOptions::http_upstream_request_policy to automatically sanitize upstream headers.

de192b77f545721a:2469.summary: Researchers have developed GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that exposes how large reasoning models perform fine-grained image localization by extracting small, distinctive visual clues. Evaluating GeoTrace on a worldwide benchmark of 525 ordinary images revealed that Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-5-mini could localize 25.71% and 16.95% of images within 1 km, respectively. To counteract this privacy risk, the authors created GeoShift, a proactive defense mechanism that preserves broad scene properties while altering high-impact geo-revealing clues. Experiments demonstrate that GeoShift reduces street-level localization accuracy down to 2.48% for GPT-5-mini and 3.81% for Gemini-3-Flash without degrading overall visual quality.

ac0829ae63dfb2e0:2011.summary: To handle uncertain job arrivals and mitigate nonlinear tardiness in dynamic scheduling, researchers propose an Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP) framework that uses a pretrained large language model as an exogenous world model. 02cffdc1f91ec71f:2528.summary: Researchers introduced a trace-level divergence framework to evaluate multilingual large language models by comparing visible reasoning traces as structured sequences rather than just final answers. dd176cb7dce46a22:4504.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-79982, has been discovered in the Bluetooth HCI USB transport class of Zephyr's new USB device stack (subsys/usb/device_next/class/bt_hci.c). The flaw involves an out-of-bounds write occurring when a controller-to-host HCI packet exceeds the bulk endpoint maximum packet size of 64 bytes. Because the transfer buffer is allocated from a fixed pool (bt_hci_ep_pool) without boundary validation in net_buf_add_mem(), oversized packets—such as mandatory 70-byte initialization commands or malicious over-the-air fragments—overflow into adjacent memory slots. On production builds with assertions disabled (CONFIG_ASSERT=n), this silently corrupts memory and can lead to arbitrary code execution by an unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range; with assertions enabled, it causes a denial of service via system panic. The fix introduces a properly sized separate pool, bt_hci_tx_pool, to handle controller-to-host packets.

056e69b89b8bf2a6:2394.summary: To resolve the paradox where supervised models generalize poorly to out-of-distribution (OoD) attacks and unsupervised models experience high false-alarm rates, researchers introduced a Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble for cybersecurity anomaly detection on the BETH kernel-level dataset. The framework combines a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier to handle known insider threats with a parallel Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) module to detect geometric anomalies. The approach achieved a state-of-the-art AUROC of 0.9951 on the BETH test set.

ff6f68426a988fe3:3248.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-58202, exists in OpenReception appointment booking software prior to version 2.0.0, where account confirmation links in emails are constructed from the unvalidated request Host header rather than a trusted tenant domain. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via the POST /api/auth/resend-confirmation endpoint by injecting a malicious Host header alongside a pending invitee's email address. When the invitee clicks the password/account confirmation link generated in the resulting email, the one-time token is sent directly to the attacker. The attacker can then complete the account registration on the legitimate tenant domain and register an attacker-controlled passkey to fully hijack the account before the victim can use it. The issue can be mitigated via front proxy restrictions or updated to version 2.0.0.

72dee010971cff31:2891.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-115895, has been identified in Happy DOM versions 17.0.0 through 21.0.4. The flaw stems from an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943 within `packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts`, where named ECMAScript module import aliases are accepted without validating if they are valid JavaScript binding identifiers before insertion into generated destructuring bindings. When JavaScript evaluation is enabled, an attacker can supply malicious HTML or module sources with invalid aliases that compile into valid default initializers, resulting in arbitrary code execution in the Node.js host process. The vulnerability can be triggered via JSON module import attributes and is patched in version 21.0.4.

6666dbd1ec16281e:3325.summary: WordPress plugin aBlocks up to version 2.17.0 contains an authenticated privilege escalation vulnerability via its registration REST endpoint (`/ablocks/v1/form-builder/registration`). The endpoint is registered with `__return_true` permission callbacks and directly reads `roleSlug` parameters from untrusted block attributes without verifying that the form type is set to registration during execution. This allows an attacker with Contributor-level access to manipulate block attributes, bypass save-time checks, and elevate their account to an Editor role through `WP_User::set_role()` and session cookie generation. 23645b983b014ff2:9472.summary: Sonar Research argues that AI model routing should be treated as a quality control mechanism rather than just a cost-saving lever. Current routing strategies often flatten performance into a single metric, ignoring critical dimensions like security, functional correctness, reliability, and maintainability. Research shows that models diverge significantly in these areas, with some producing higher rates of security debt or runtime defects despite similar aggregate benchmarks. The industry is encouraged to match model capability to the specific criticality of the task, such as using frontier models for security-sensitive code while utilizing lower-tier models for routine work.
23645b983b014ff2:9472.one_liner: Stop routing all code to frontier models; you need to account for security and maintainability debt, not just cost and latency.
23645b983b014ff2:9472.bottom_line: Effective AI coding strategy requires routing tasks based on specific quality dimensions like security and reliability rather than defaulting to the most expensive model.

14d2b3640a647b73:16285.summary: Research into LLM jailbreaks demonstrates that these attacks are prompt-level manipulations rather than model defects, meaning they cannot be permanently patched through fine-tuning or weight adjustments. A study using 32 malicious prompts showed that attackers can achieve near-perfect success rates by selecting the most effective attack strategy for a given model. Because the space of possible prompts is open-ended, security teams must focus on measuring attack success rates against specific model versions rather than seeking a universal fix. The research highlights that jailbreaks are an inherent property of how models are instructed to follow conflicting directives.
14d2b3640a647b73:16285.one_liner: Jailbreaks are prompt-level exploits that cannot be 'fixed' in the model weights, requiring a shift toward system-level security and monitoring.
14d2b3640a647b73:16285.bottom_line: Stop treating jailbreaks as bugs to be patched and start treating them as an inevitable, ongoing risk that requires robust input validation and output monitoring.

077ef200d3e00808:6620.summary: A sophisticated UEFI bootkit dubbed BlackX has been deployed against diplomatic entities in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan, orchestrated by the China-linked APT41 group. The malware is an updated version of BlackLotus and exploits the patched Secure Boot bypass vulnerability CVE-2022-21894 (Baton Drop) to load malicious code before the OS starts. b4f089d23ad80a59:3363.summary: Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, face two remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative that were disclosed publicly without prior mainline kernel fixes. The second flaw, ZDI-CAN-33774, enables unauthenticated pre-authentication attacks over port 445 due to a handler table assignment race condition. 91e38cb5730dbf2e:5707.summary: Traditional cybersecurity policies rely on database encryption, network security, and access controls, but fail to protect data once decrypted and processed across cloud platforms, analytics tools, and AI pipelines. Because data must be read to be used, breaches or future quantum decryption can expose sensitive plaintext information. To mitigate this risk without stalling operations, policymakers and organizations are turning to vaultless, keyless pseudonymization. This approach replaces sensitive identifiers like names, social security numbers, and payment cards with structurally valid substitutes, eliminating central vaults as single points of failure and rendering stolen data useless to threat actors.

91e38cb5730dbf2e:5707.bottom_line: Encryption leaves decrypted data vulnerable during processing, making vaultless pseudonymization necessary to strip stolen data of its value.

810b29c71de73a3b:6952.summary: While India's electric vehicle transition has made commendable progress in material recycling and scrappage infrastructure—processing 4.3 lakh vehicles across 129 registered scrapping facilities by January 2026—it overlooks the critical role of asset reuse. Circular economy principles dictate a hierarchy prioritizing reduction and reuse over raw recycling. Vehicle retrofitment, which replaces internal combustion engines with electric powertrains while preserving structurally sound chassis and body frames, offers a viable middle path. Scaling retrofitment across India's massive vehicle fleet could prevent massive volumes of recycling and landfill waste.

Operating out-of-band on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs as part of the NVIDIA OpenShell reference architecture, Sentry runs in a hardware trust domain entirely outside the agent's reach to prevent compromised agents from altering their restrictions. 3bf316beeb9aa0eb:4248.summary: A high-severity soundness bug, tracked as CVE-2026-72703 with a CVSS score of 7.1, has been identified in the kernel guard checker of the Rocq (formerly Coq) proof assistant versions 8.20 through less than 9.2.0. The vulnerability arises because the find_uniform_parameters function fails to examine cross-calls within mutual fixpoints when no self-recursive calls are present, allowing the checker to accept non-terminating recursive definitions. This enables the construction of checked proofs of arbitrary propositions, including False and 0 = 1, undermining formal verification guarantees in certified software and compilers. Users are advised to upgrade to version 9.2.0 or later.

34b1f6d3e02dc582:5979.summary: A zero-day kernel soundness vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-72714, affects the Rocq proof assistant by desynchronizing the universe checking state after closing a local module. Specifically, when a module locally disables universe checking (`Local Unset Universe Checking`), the global flag is restored but the universe graph retains the disabled state. This permits Hurkens' paradox to derive False, allowing the creation of certified mathematical forgeries for Millennium Problems—such as the Riemann Hypothesis and P=NP—that successfully pass proof verification checks with clean axiom whitelists.

130115baab528e50:5285.summary: A long-standing soundness vulnerability in the Rocq (formerly Coq) proof assistant allows the construction of a proof of 'False' that bypasses integrity checks. The issue occurs when the module system inlines parameters, causing the system to drop metadata that tracks unsafe universe checking. Consequently, the 'Print Assumptions' command incorrectly reports these proofs as closed and axiom-free, undermining the trust model for formally verified systems. This bug has remained unfixed since 2020 and affects critical verification chains like CompCert and CertiKOS.

081b42e7e35750b4:1973.summary: Researchers have introduced PEAR, an adaptive advantage reshaping method designed to improve perception and exploration in large vision-language models. Effective multimodal reasoning requires models to utilize visual information while thoroughly exploring diverse reasoning paths, but existing methods scaling token entropy by visual dependency can underweigh high-entropy tokens. PEAR maintains visual dependency as a base signal while adding an entropy-based exploration gain specifically at high-entropy positions, giving lower visual dependency a larger additional boost. Experiments conducted on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B models demonstrate that PEAR achieves superior average performance across multimodal reasoning benchmarks alongside strong results in general tasks.

623258d9f2722ae2:2488.summary: Distilling interactive LLM agents requires choosing between teacher demonstrations and student experiences, corresponding to off-policy and on-policy training. This study argues that this distinction is hierarchical, as the policy inducing interaction history can differ from the policy generating action prefixes. Researchers introduced a hierarchical agent distillation framework to explicitly control these two levels of on-policiness across three models and four interactive environments. The findings show that student-induced histories paired with teacher-generated action prefixes provide the strongest standalone training signal, whereas fully on-policy data is most effective when mixed with other configurations. Additionally, front-loading teacher contexts and delaying fully on-policy contexts improves over static mixtures.

623258d9f2722ae2:2488.bottom_line: Optimizing LLM agent distillation requires separating history generation from action prefixes, with student histories paired with teacher actions yielding the best standalone results.

998635a9e8d70175:1341.summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-54630, has been discovered in Part-DB, an open-source inventory management system for electronic components prior to version 2.12.1. The flaw exists in the part attachment upload handler, which stores uploaded files using client-supplied extensions and fails to include phar in its extension blocklist. Because public attachments are written directly into the Apache document root under public/media/, and Apache is configured to route .phar files to PHP-FPM, authenticated users in the default users group can upload malicious .phar files. e198514b0edb5476:2579.summary: Multi-stage analytical tasks require LLM agents to use intermediate evidence to decide whether to continue, redirect, or stop. Although self-reflection evaluates agent output, it often fails to verify whether intermediate evidence actively changes subsequent actions—a capability researchers term self-restraint. To evaluate this, researchers introduced DMAIC-Bench, incorporating 97 seeded tasks across 15 industrial cases and life-sciences sectors with explicit statistical prerequisites. Evaluations across 13 models revealed an average execution routing accuracy of 92% on matched GO decisions, but only 19% on NO-GO decisions, with blinded expert reviews estimating that models act on invalid evidence in 47% of reached NO-GO decisions.

7a69dd3801c98c9b:2080.summary: AI researchers examine the problem of skill internalization in LLM agent hubs, where models acquire capabilities natively and no longer require retrieved public skills. 864b2d1b92f976c6:2565.summary: Researchers have introduced AquaSense-ICS, a hybrid real-simulated dataset and benchmark designed for smart water quality monitoring and cyber-attack detection in industrial control systems. The dataset combines 25.4 hours of physical recording from a Raspberry Pi 5 edge node using TDS and BME680 sensors with a 13-node looped network simulated in EPANET-MSX, incorporating parameterized cyber-attacks and sensor faults. Benchmarking results demonstrate that standard random row splits yield misleadingly high performance due to data leakage, whereas a strict chronological and leakage-aware evaluation protocol drops model detection capabilities significantly, proving that existing machine learning models leave substantial headroom for improvement.

864b2d1b92f976c6:2565.bottom_line: Random-split evaluations on water cyber-physical system datasets yield falsely inflated performance, while leakage-aware protocols reveal significant vulnerabilities in current attack detection models.

646f70f96a170b82:2531.summary: Researchers have introduced Self-Direction, a mechanism that allows AI agents to learn from failures by extracting lessons into lightweight low-rank adapters while keeping base model weights frozen. 3dd848a61e0f962e:2609.summary: A study investigating LLM vulnerability auditors reveals that models exhibit asymmetric deference to static-analysis evidence, placing excessive trust in false assurances while scrutinizing false alarms. While standard prompt instructions failed to reduce this deference, verifying claims in a separate call and showing refuted claims raised accuracy by 12 points under false assurances. The findings indicate that security pipelines must independently verify static analyzer guarantees before allowing LLMs to rely on them.
3dd848a61e0f962e:2609.one_liner: LLM vulnerability auditors place dangerous trust in false static-analysis assurances, missing real flaws unless analyzer outputs are independently verified first.
3dd848a61e0f962e:2609.bottom_line: Security pipelines combining LLMs with static analysis must independently verify tool guarantees because models disproportionately trust false assurances while ignoring real vulnerabilities.

6b938a479679dd85:2470.summary: Edge-cloud split multimodal LLM architectures transmit intermediate features to servers to reduce on-device computation, but this exposes user privacy because servers can infer sensitive attributes like age, gender, and race from those features. To evaluate this leakage rigorously, researchers propose a label-budgeted attribute-inference framework using recovery curves that measure how much information an honest-but-curious server can reconstruct given a specific labeled-sample budget. Evaluations show that unprotected pipelines leak all three attributes across split depths, and even defense mechanisms like Safe-LLaVA—which blocks biometric content in text responses—fail to prevent leakage; just 20 labeled samples per class can recover 75% to 85% of unprotected leakage from transmitted features. The findings highlight the need for privacy defenses that operate directly on transmitted intermediate representations rather than final outputs.
6b938a479679dd85:2470.one_liner: Edge-cloud split MLLMs leak sensitive user attributes through transmitted intermediate features even when response-level privacy filters are active.
6b938a479679dd85:2470.bottom_line: Response-level privacy filters are insufficient for split multimodal LLMs because an honest-but-curious server can reconstruct sensitive attributes from intermediate feature transmissions using minimal labeled samples.

d6271ea16694ab42:2749.summary: Researchers have developed KnotScryer, a tool to detect compositional security risks in AI agents that combine multiple individually clean third-party skills. The vulnerability arises not from isolated skills, but from runtime orchestration where an agent passes an upstream skill's output to a downstream skill's input, forming safety-violation chains. KnotScryer abstracts skills into capability summaries, builds a Skill Capability-Flow Graph, tracks untrusted data along edges, and uses a two-layer verification method with reachability analysis and an LLM chain audit. Analyzing 13,598 skills from ClawHub across multiple frameworks, KnotScryer identified 612 insecure compositions, demonstrating that 13.7% of detected violation chains consist entirely of skills marked safe by single-skill scanners.
d6271ea16694ab42:2749.one_liner: KnotScryer detects insecure security chains in AI agents caused by combining individually safe third-party skills into dangerous capability flows.
d6271ea16694ab42:2749.bottom_line: AI agent architectures must account for compositional security risks because individually safe third-party skills can be chained together into safety violations at runtime.

claims.text: To this end, we develop KnotScryer to detect insecure skill compositions by treating skills as typed capability flows.
claims.support_span: To this end, we develop KnotScryer to detect insecure skill compositions by treating skills as typed capability flows.

claims.text: Furthermore, 13.7% of the detected chains consist entirely of skills labeled safe by a single-skill scanner, showing that KnotScryer effectively identifies insecure compositions that per-skill auditing cannot.
claims.support_span: Furthermore, 13.7% of the detected chains consist entirely of skills labeled safe by a single-skill scanner, showing that KnotScryer effectively identifies insecure compositions that per-skill auditing cannot.

67f7390a0de3208c:2281.summary: Large language models often fall into an information trap when making decisions under incomplete information, paying for costly evidence that cannot change their decision or continuing to query when evidence is already sufficient. To address this, researchers propose Decision-Informed Value-of-information Acquisition (DIVA), a training-free procedure that has the LLM specify a simple decision model and evaluates candidate checks by their net decision value. DIVA stops acquiring information once no further check is worth its cost. Experiments across four domains and 20 LLMs demonstrate that the DIVA-U variant achieves lower regret than standard LLM baselines and cuts the regret of the best baseline by 75% in synthetic scenarios.
67f7390a0de3208c:2281.one_liner: DIVA prevents LLMs from wasting compute on redundant information gathering by valuing information checks based on their direct impact on decision outcomes.
67f7390a0de3208c:2281.bottom_line: LLM agent efficiency in decision-making under uncertainty can be vastly improved by evaluating information checks through decision-value models rather than unconstrained querying.

claims.text: To this end, we propose Decision-Informed Value-of-information Acquisition (DIVA), a simple yet effective procedure for LLM information seeking based on the decision value of evidence.
claims.support_span: To this end, we propose Decision-Informed Value-of-information Acquisition (DIVA), a simple yet effective procedure for LLM information seeking based on the decision value of evidence.

claims.text: Across four domains and 20 LLMs, DIVA-U has lower regret, i.e., value lost relative to the best possible decision, than every LLM baseline on real-world data, mainly by stopping once evidence suffices, and DIVA cuts the regret of the best LLM baseline by 75% in synthetic scenarios where every check's reliability is given.
claims.support_span: Across four domains and 20 LLMs, DIVA-U has lower regret, i.e., value lost relative to the best possible decision, than every LLM baseline on real-world data, mainly by stopping once evidence suffices, and DIVA cuts the regret of the best LLM baseline by 75% in synthetic scenarios where every check's reliability is given.

05ae973a07760e7d:1927.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-115825, has been disclosed in HTTP::Server::PSGI (Plack) for Perl prior to version 1.0056. Because Perl pre-allocates the read buffer to match the requested size before any body bytes arrive, the server encounters an out-of-memory error and exits. Maintainers have released version 1.0057 to address this memory allocation vector.

d9e25ae2821aa8b4:2493.summary: A vulnerability has been identified in the compress zstd library prior to version 1.20.2, where crafted two-block frames cause a panic in huff0.ReadTable. 94d51fe2d20419a9:7769.summary: Dutch security firm Eye Security executed 'Operation IXIM' between November 2025 and March 2026, pushing over 2 million background updates to unowned computers to disable an unpatched vulnerability in the abandoned Popcorn Time media streaming application. 6d46166b653f8b22:1903.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems often fail due to communication issues rather than isolated first-round errors, leading researchers to build a corpus-grounded taxonomy across 3,211 trajectories. The study reveals that recovery and consensus problems dominate, with agents frequently converging too early, ignoring dissent, or preserving wrong framing after observing peer responses. To mitigate these issues, the authors recommend incorporating stronger disagreement handling, evidence verification, and minority-signal preservation before finalization. These findings highlight the need for robust orchestration layers to prevent premature consensus in automated multi-agent reasoning tasks.
6d46166b653f8b22:1903.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM systems fail primarily from consensus and recovery errors rather than bad first-round ideas, requiring stronger disagreement handling.
6d46166b653f8b22:1903.bottom_line: Multi-agent LLM systems must implement rigorous disagreement handling and minority-signal preservation to prevent premature consensus and reasoning failures.

claims.text: We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks.
claims.support_span: We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks.

claims.text: We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses.
claims.support_span: We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses.

0ea7735a7fe290e9:2215.summary: Researchers introduce ALTO, an open-source training recipe for the 20-billion-parameter GPT-OSS-20B mixture-of-experts model under the MXFP4 microscaling format to reduce quantization error in sub-8-bit arithmetic. By combining hybrid block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, stochastic rounding, and a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme, the model achieves a validation loss of 3.3350 on C4. This result closes roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation and brings convergence overhead down from +20.0% to +5.0% compared to a BF16 baseline. All experiments utilized simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300 hardware.

0ea7735a7fe290e9:2215.bottom_line: De-oscillation and advanced quantization techniques can successfully stabilize 4-bit training, reducing FP4 convergence overhead to just 5.0% over BF16.

6448f4db86e014bd:2366.summary: Researchers investigating repeated multi-party LLM negotiations discovered a significant "trust-agreement gap" where accurate trust estimates do not automatically yield better agreements. While trust-aware agents can successfully identify malicious adversaries within a few rounds, explicit trust only increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points when agents are actively guided to incorporate trust into their decision-making. The study utilized a framework where recurring agents engage in sequential negotiations with a covert adversary attempting to block consensus. These findings indicate that agent frameworks require deliberate instruction regarding how to process reputation and historical interactions to achieve collaborative goals.
6448f4db86e014bd:2366.one_liner: LLM agents can identify adversaries through trust tracking, but explicit guidance is required to translate trust into successful negotiation outcomes.
6448f4db86e014bd:2366.bottom_line: Accurate trust estimation in multi-agent negotiations fails to improve agreement rates unless agents are explicitly programmed to use trust in decision-making.

claims.text: Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements.
claims.support_span: Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements.

claims.text: Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions.
claims.support_span: Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions.

6ba5f7a7c750d7d9:2605.summary: Tencent researchers have introduced TGR-EvoDAG, a multi-agent code evolution framework designed for generative recommendation pipelines that models code changes as a Directed Acyclic Graph. Generative recommendation relies on multi-stage pipelines where standard recursive self-improvement methods suffer from cost blindness and short-sighted evaluation. TGR-EvoDAG solves this by incorporating stage-aware cost planning to optimize GPU budgets and active downstream co-adaptation to navigate temporary metric regressions. In industrial deployment on Tencent's commercial media platform, the framework achieved a 12.16% relative improvement in offline Hit@1 and a 0.40% increase in online click-through rate.
6ba5f7a7c750d7d9:2605.one_liner: Tencent's DAG-based multi-agent evolution framework optimizes generative recommendation pipelines and boosts online click-through rates.
6ba5f7a7c750d7d9:2605.bottom_line: TGR-EvoDAG successfully automates multi-stage recommendation code evolution, delivering a statistically significant click-through rate increase in production.

b895b5b92f31fb61:2672.summary: Researchers propose a physically grounded multimodal agent architecture featuring three independent components to control scientific instruments with nonstationary responses, such as neutral beam injection ion sources in magnetic confinement fusion devices. The system uses deterministic algorithms to extract symbolic physical quantities and visual evidence from multichannel waveforms, a multi-layered memory system to organize trajectories, and an independent action feasibility check to enforce constraints before model execution. Evaluated across 455 historical shots from EXL-50U platforms, physical symbols outperformed raw waveform images in quality classification, and context retrieval significantly improved agreement with historical tuning directions. Under supervised operation on five ion sources, the framework achieved a beam-extraction rate of 86.80% across 409 executed shots.

b895b5b92f31fb61:2672.bottom_line: Multimodal agents integrating deterministic physical symbol extraction and memory can reliably manage nonstationary scientific instrument tuning.

9425229b133727b8:1685.summary: Evaluating production conversational agents on live enterprise data is challenging because backend state changes and data drift invalidate static benchmarks over time. To solve this, researchers developed an offline evaluation harness that remains reproducible despite mutating data and can be regenerated on demand. Using this harness as a fitness function alongside GEPA-based prompt optimization and a correctness gate, they successfully compressed a production merchant-facing agent's prompt surface by 3.5% to 7.6%. This reduction was achieved without regressing task correctness across three independent subject-model families, with one model showing measurable performance improvements.
9425229b133727b8:1685.one_liner: A reproducible offline evaluation harness enables safe, correctness-gated prompt compression for production conversational agents.
9425229b133727b8:1685.bottom_line: Correctness-gated prompt optimization driven by a drift-resilient evaluation harness safely reduces production agent prompt size without hurting task accuracy.

claims.text: Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

59c212f8d15219b6:2040.summary: Researchers introduce DriveMind, an MLLM-based autonomous driving framework that maintains multiple simultaneous scene interpretations using belief tracking inspired by particle filtering. Traditional MLLM drivers process frames from scratch and commit to a single hypothesis, frequently leading to catastrophic errors in ambiguous traffic conditions. DriveMind propagates multiple hypotheses through a vision-language model, scores them against current observations, and resamples them to preserve diversity. On the Bench2Drive benchmark, this approach improves the overall Driving Score from 68.50 to 81.37 and raises the Success Rate from 41.36% to 54.09%, with substantial gains in tricky scenarios like unsignalized intersections.
59c212f8d15219b6:2040.one_liner: DriveMind uses particle-filtering-inspired belief tracking to let multimodal LLM drivers evaluate multiple scene hypotheses simultaneously.
59c212f8d15219b6:2040.bottom_line: Tracking multiple simultaneous scene hypotheses drastically improves autonomous driving safety and success rates in ambiguous traffic scenarios.

25ad350bf057290f:2261.summary: To address systematic confusion between semantically adjacent emotions in multimodal emotion recognition models, researchers propose Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution (CASE), an agent-skill framework that externalizes affective expertise. Rather than adjusting global model parameters, CASE maintains a sparse, self-evolving library of pair-specific EmotionSkills that are dynamically retrieved during inference to reinforce boundary-aware reasoning while keeping the underlying MLLM backbone frozen. Experiments across CA-MER, DFEW, and EMER benchmarks demonstrate that CASE improves model performance and transfers effectively across diverse backbones. Notably, CASE boosts the average accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B on the CA-MER benchmark from 46.80% to 59.13%.

25ad350bf057290f:2261.bottom_line: Externalizing affective expertise into retrievable agent skills successfully improves emotion recognition accuracy across frozen MLLM backbones.

claims.support_span: Notably, CASE improves the average accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B on the CA-MER benchmark from 46.80% to 59.13%, while achieving consistent gains across MLLMs.

52e1ba098aca08c7:2125.summary: Researchers introduce MemCryst, a lifelong context adaptation framework that coordinates the bidirectional learning of memory and skills for LLM agents within a bounded context window. While memory supplies past factual experiences and skills provide reusable procedures, MemCryst treats them jointly: recurring episodes drive skill creation, and skills generate new memory records for subsequent learning. Furthermore, task outcomes adjust the retrieval influence of records without altering their core content. Across ten diverse settings, MemCryst outperforms memory-only or skill-only configurations, achieving a 63.17% success rate on ALFWorld compared to 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only approaches.
52e1ba098aca08c7:2125.one_liner: MemCryst coordinates bidirectional learning between memory and skills to improve lifelong adaptation in LLM agents.
52e1ba098aca08c7:2125.bottom_line: Jointly serving retrieved memory and learned skills with dynamic outcome-based weighting significantly enhances lifelong LLM agent performance.
